39	  - review_lenses
40	  - review-aggregator
41	  - pr
42	
43	# ─── always_run (#1831) ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────
44	# Stages that run on EVERY exit path — success, non-zero rc, SIGINT, SIGTERM,
45	# timeout — in the order listed, after the flow has ended.
46	#
47	# This replaces a hardcoded dispatch in the runner's EXIT trap, which named one
48	# plugin by DIRECTORY (`plugins/tool/teardown`) and degraded silently to a no-op
49	# if it was absent. "Runs on every exit path" is a property of the FLOW, so it
50	# belongs in the template that defines the flow — not at a line number inside a
51	# 3000-line runner, where an edit can drop it without anything noticing. #1878
52	# found exactly that failure in the sibling mechanism: the snapshot was never
53	# called.
54	#
55	# An always-run stage is NOT part of `flow:` and never enters the flow's stage
56	# list: it has no place in the pipeline's data dependencies and must not affect
57	# convergence, verdicts, or the run's exit status.
58	#
59	# Each entry is an ordinary top-level stage section — resolved by `roles:` like
60	# any other stage, and bounded by its own `router.timeout_s`. A name here with
61	# no section, or a section with no `roles:`, REFUSES the template rather than
62	# quietly running nothing.
63	always_run:
64	  - release
65	  - persist
66	
67	# ─── delivery_loop (cycle) — #2271, ADR-068 ─────────────────────────────────
68	# One outer loop holds the design loop and the build loop. Every stage sees
69	# every finding and says in its own result what it did about each; the engine
70	# never decides who owns a finding, and nothing jumps backwards.
71	#   - A design loop that runs out of rounds ends this round (build is skipped)
72	#     and this loop goes round. When this loop's rounds are spent, the run stops.
73	delivery_loop:
74	  type: cycle
75	  description: Design, then build, until both pass — going round when a finding needs design
76	  flow:
77	    - design_verify_cycle
78	    - build_test_cycle
79	  exit_when:
80	    all:
81	      - { stage: design_verify_cycle, field: verdict, op: eq, value: pass }
82	      - { stage: build_test_cycle, field: verdict, op: eq, value: pass }
83	  max_iterations: 2
84	  on_max: halt
85	
86	# ─── design_verify_cycle (cycle) ─────────────────────────────────────────────
87	# ADR-046 (#1218, EPIC #1216): give the design stage an independent verifier that
88	# loops back TO it BEFORE the build cycle — so design/contract defects are caught
89	# where they are authored, not deep in the build cycle. Modelled on standard.yaml's
90	# design_impact_cycle (standard.yaml:40-67), which simple.yaml historically lacked.
91	#
92	# Members: design → design-gate. design-gate is a T0 tool (ADR-037 §3): a pure-grep
93	# PRE-build structural gate over design.md + the red-first stubs design writes. It
94	# is BOTH a cycle member AND convergence:gate, so the typed-aggregator preflight
95	# rule (A) is satisfied by binding exit_when directly to it — a single gate, no
96	# separate aggregator needed (contrast build_test_cycle's gate-aggregator, which
97	# rolls up MANY gates). exit_when fires on design-gate.verdict == pass.
98	# max_iterations: 2, on_max: halt (#2176): a contract the gate still rejects is
99	# not built. Nested in delivery_loop (#2271), running out of rounds ends that
100	# loop's round — build is skipped — and the outer loop goes round.
101	#
102	# Feedback: design.design → design.prior_design (self-edge) — mirrors
103	# design_impact_cycle so iter N+1 refines rather than re-creates (#773 lesson).
104	#
105	design_verify_cycle:
106	  type: cycle
107	  description: Verify the design contract is build-ready until design-gate passes
108	  flow:
109	    - design
110	    # #1683: does the design cover what the ISSUE asked for? Design is the only
111	    # reader of the issue, so nothing else confirms the SPECs are a faithful
112	    # statement of the ask. Inside the cycle, so a finding reaches design itself
113	    # on the next iteration.
114	    - spec-coverage
115	    - design-gate
116	  # #1284/ADR-047 multi-condition: BOTH must hold. spec-coverage may gate under
117	  # ADR-040 §5 as amended by #2040 — the standard it judges against is the
118	  # ISSUE, which design cannot re-author, so the only way to converge is to
119	  # actually cover it.
120	  #
121	  # `ne uncovered` rather than `eq covered`: `unreadable` must not stall the
122	  # cycle. intake writes a placeholder when the issue fetch fails (#1804), and
123	  # failing closed there would break every offline run for a condition that is
124	  # not design's fault. The finding still ships in the summary.
125	  exit_when:
126	    all:
127	      - { stage: design-gate, field: verdict, op: eq, value: pass }
128	      - { stage: spec-coverage, field: verdict, op: ne, value: uncovered }
129	  max_iterations: 2
130	  on_max: halt
131	  feedback:
132	    - from:
133	        stage: design
134	        output: design
135	      to:
136	        stage: design
137	        input: design
138	        required: false
139	
140	# ─── spec-coverage (leaf, gate) ──────────────────────────────────────────────
141	# Model-judged but admissible on the convergence path (ADR-040 §5 / #2040): its
142	# standard is the issue, produced by intake OUTSIDE this cycle, so the judged
143	# party cannot re-author it.
144	spec-coverage:
145	  gate: auto
146	  roles: [spec_coverage]
147	  # A product owner asks "was what was asked for delivered?" — intent-seeking,
148	  # which is wrong for judging an assertion against a SPEC (the bug there
149	  # survives charity) and exactly right here, where the question IS about intent.
150	  persona: product-owner
151	  router:
152	    timeout_s: 600
153	
154	# ─── test-author (leaf, advisory) ────────────────────────────────────────────
155	# ADR-040 §5: it makes a model call, so it may not sit on the convergence path.
156	# Its work is verified mechanically downstream — the test stage runs the
157	# assertions and acceptance-gate proves they discriminate.
158	test-author:
159	  gate: auto
160	  roles: [test_author]
161	  # #2188: no authored assertions → the cycle stops before build. Otherwise build
162	  # writes its own tests, the defect #2022 exists to prevent (#1849 run
163	  # 35949629759). Its failure is retried first (the stage's `retry:` budget).
164	  blocking: true
165	  router:
166	    # #2188: the same budget as build — authoring a 15–25 SPEC contract is
167	    # build-sized work (#1849: two 600s calls both timed out mid-write).
168	    # #2225: per CALL now — test-author loops until it says it is done, like
169	    # build, so a big contract takes more calls instead of overrunning one.
170	    # At most 4 calls: timeouts that are not back-to-back let the loop go on,
171	    # so the ceiling is calls × timeout — 60 min here (review #2229).
172	    timeout_s: 900
173	    max_turns: 0
174	    max_iterations: 4
175	
176	# ─── spec-correspondence (leaf, advisory) ────────────────────────────────────
177	# ADR-040 §5: it makes a model call, so it may not gate. Its finding reaches
178	# test-author on the next iteration through the summary channel.
179	spec-correspondence:
180	  gate: auto
181	  roles: [spec_correspondence]
182	  # #1627: personas were consumed only by review lenses and NO template carried
183	  # a persona: key, so a persona manifest resolved to nothing. This is the first
184	  # stage-level binding. QA assures traceability; it does not test — which is
185	  # what separates it from test-strategist, whose instinct shown a mismatched
186	  # assertion is to repair it and answer yes.
187	  persona: quality-assurance
188	  router:
189	    timeout_s: 600
190	
191	# ─── assertion-integrity (leaf, gate) ────────────────────────────────────────
192	# Mechanical, no model.route — so it MAY gate (ADR-040 §5).
193	assertion-integrity:
194	  gate: auto
195	  roles: [assertion_integrity]
196	
197	# ─── issue-acceptance (leaf, gate) ───────────────────────────────────────────
198	# #1849: the finished change against the ISSUE. A model call on the convergence
199	# path is allowed for the same reason as spec-coverage (ADR-040 §5 as amended by
200	# #2040): its standard is the issue, which the judged stages cannot re-author.
201	issue-acceptance:
202	  gate: auto
203	  roles: [issue_acceptance]
204	  # Same question spec-coverage asks of the design — "was what was asked for
205	  # delivered?" — now asked of the code.
206	  persona: product-owner
207	  router:
208	    timeout_s: 600
209	
210	# ─── build_test_cycle (cycle) ────────────────────────────────────────────────
211	# B6 (#1138, ADR-040 §2/§5): the cycle re-runs build/test then the decomposed
212	# mechanical gates (shape-floor, acceptance-gate, secret-scan) and finally the
213	# gate-aggregator, which collapses every must-pass gate into ONE convergence
214	# verdict. exit_when fires on gate-aggregator.verdict == pass — the ADR-019
215	# fail-closed contract re-expressed as a single composable construct (ADR-040 §5).
216	# (#1129 Change C, ADR-012: the lint/coverage/mutation read-out gates were
217	# DROPPED as cycle members — they were redundant. mutation and lint both run in
218	# the test suite (run-tests.sh --tier all / npm test, which the `test` cycle
219	# member runs), so a lint or mutation regression fails the `test` gate directly.
220	# coverage is NOT folded into the suite — it stays enforced by the dedicated CI
221	# `coverage` job (re-running it inside --tier all would trip the #983 re-entrancy
222	# guard; see ADR-012 "Coverage gating"). The lint-gate/coverage-gate/mutation-gate
223	# plugins remain canonical (ADR-013) but dormant for future reuse.)
224	# The individual gates are NON-blocking (no blocking:true):
225	# they emit verdict-in-artifact (ADR-004) and the cycle iterates-to-fix; the loop
226	# converges via exit_when, never via per-gate hard-blocks. max_iterations: 3.
227	# Nested in delivery_loop (#2271): running out of rounds hands back to that loop,
228	# which goes round from design.
229	build_test_cycle:
230	  type: cycle
231	  description: Build, test, and run the mechanical gates until gate-aggregator passes
232	  flow:
233	    # #2022: test-author runs FIRST. It authors the acceptance assertions from
234	    # the design's SPEC sentences before build implements against them, so the
235	    # code and the assertion are two independent readings rather than two
236	    # artifacts of one. It never sees the diff.
237	    - test-author
238	    # #2034: judges whether each assertion tests what its SPEC SAYS — the one
239	    # link execution cannot reach (a passing test proves the implementation
240	    # satisfies the ASSERTION, never that the assertion satisfies the SENTENCE).
241	    # Before build, because its question needs the requirement and the assertion
242	    # and not the implementation — which at this point does not exist yet, so
243	    # its isolation is a fact of placement rather than a rule to enforce.
244	    - spec-correspondence
245	    - build
246	    - test
247	    - shape-floor
248	    - acceptance-gate
249	    - secret-scan
250	    # #2022: mechanical backstop. The spawn denies build Edit() on the declared
251	    # TESTFILES, but #1919 P5 measured that a Write(...) deny rule matches
252	    # nothing — prevention is incomplete by construction. A fail here makes the
253	    # aggregate non-pass, so the cycle iterates rather than converging on a
254	    # rewritten assertion.
255	    - assertion-integrity
256	    # #1849: the finished change judged against the ISSUE, not the SPECs — the
257	    # only check after spec-coverage that reads the issue at all. A convergence
258	    # gate, so gate-aggregator's roster makes it must-pass; each unmet
259	    # requirement is a numbered finding.
260	    - issue-acceptance
261	    - gate-aggregator
262	  exit_when:
263	    stage: gate-aggregator
264	    field: verdict
265	    op: eq
266	    value: pass
267	  max_iterations: 3
268	  on_max: continue
269	  # The cycle CONVERGES rather than spinning build(no-op)→…→gate-aggregator(fail)
270	  # because the aggregator's consolidated gate-feedback.md reaches build. B2
271	  # (ADR-040): the gate-aggregator is the SINGLE collector of failure detail,
272	  # merging every failing mechanical gate into one document. It used to arrive
273	  # through a feedback: wire plus a bespoke reader; #1979 retired both — the
274	  # aggregator marks that output `summary: true` (#1976) and the engine injects
275	  # it, framed by verdict, with no per-consumer wiring.
276	# ─── intake (leaf) ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
277	intake:
278	  gate: auto
279	  roles: [intake]
280	  io:
281	    destinations: [file, stdout]
282	    tail_lines: 200
283	
284	# ─── plan (leaf) ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
285	plan:
286	  gate: auto
287	  roles: [planner]
288	  # ADR-051: the provider runs the stage as this persona (--agent).
289	  persona: product-owner
290	  io:
291	    destinations: [file, stdout]
292	    tail_lines: 200
293	  router:
294	    timeout_s: 300
295	    # 45 (raised from the 25 default, #1442) — same starvation the impact stage
296	    # hit (#impact-max-turns): scope exploration needs headroom. The planner is
297	    # also told this budget in its prompt and biased to converge before it runs out.
298	    max_turns: 45
299	
300	# ─── design (leaf, design_verify_cycle member) ───────────────────────────────
301	design:
302	  gate: auto
303	  roles: [designer]
304	  # ADR-051: the provider runs the stage as this persona (--agent).
305	  persona: architect
306	  io:
307	    destinations: [file, stdout]
308	    tail_lines: 200
309	  router:
310	    timeout_s: 600
311	    max_turns: 0
312	
313	# ─── design-gate (leaf, design_verify_cycle member) ──────────────────────────
314	# T0 tool gate (ADR-046, #1218): PRE-build mechanical structural gate. Pure grep
315	# over design.md (NO LLM, NO baseline — ADR-037 §3). Runs the 5 structural
316	# checks (scope non-empty; acceptance block well-formed; every SPEC has a status
317	# — [code], [no-code] or [done] with evidence that exists (ADR-069); every [code]
318	# SPEC declares a TESTFILE; WIRING present/none + paths exist) and reports ALL
319	# violations in ONE pass. verdict-in-artifact; the design_verify_cycle exit_when
320	# reads design-gate.verdict == pass. Bound by role design_gate.
321	design-gate:
322	  gate: auto
323	  roles: [design_gate]
324	  io:
325	    destinations: [file, stdout]
326	    tail_lines: 200
327	
328	# ─── build (leaf, cycle member) ──────────────────────────────────────────────
329	build:
330	  gate: auto
331	  roles: [builder]
332	  # ADR-051: the provider runs the stage as this persona (--agent).
333	  persona: developer
334	  io:
335	    destinations: [file, stdout]
336	    tail_lines: 200
337	  router:
338	    timeout_s: 900
339	    max_turns: 0
340	
341	# ─── test (leaf, cycle member) ───────────────────────────────────────────────
342	test:
343	  gate: auto
344	  roles: [tester]
345	  io:
346	    destinations: [file, stdout]
347	    tail_lines: 200
348	
349	# ─── shape-floor (leaf, cycle member) ────────────────────────────────────────
350	# T0 tool gate (ADR-040, #1134): un-gameable shape-floor check. verdict-in-artifact.
351	shape-floor:
352	  gate: auto
353	  roles: [shape_floor]
354	  io:
355	    destinations: [file, stdout]
356	    tail_lines: 200
357	
358	# ─── acceptance-gate (leaf, cycle member) ────────────────────────────────────
359	# Mechanical (non-LLM) acceptance-contract gate (ADR-036, #922). No-op pass when
360	# the design acceptance block is absent (its design input is required:false in the
361	# manifest — design already emits the SPEC/WIRING block). Its gate_result feeds
362	# the acceptance→build feedback edge above.
363	# ADR-036 #1188: negctl_timeout_s bounds each SPEC negative-control / reachability
364	# test run (seconds). A timeout is classified INFRA (non-terminal), never a
365	# violation. Override per-run with ZBUILD_NEGCTL_TIMEOUT (env wins).
366	acceptance-gate:
367	  gate: auto
368	  roles: [acceptance_gate]
369	  negctl_timeout_s: 60
370	  io:
371	    destinations: [file, stdout]
372	    tail_lines: 200
373	  router:
374	    timeout_s: 600
375	    max_turns: 10
376	
377	# ─── secret-scan (leaf, cycle member) ────────────────────────────────────────
378	# T0 tool gate (ADR-040, #1136): blocks hardcoded secrets/.env in the diff.
379	# verdict-in-artifact (skip on empty diff).
380	secret-scan:
381	  gate: auto
382	  roles: [secret_scan]
383	  io:
384	    destinations: [file, stdout]
385	    tail_lines: 200
386	
387	# ─── gate-aggregator (leaf, cycle member) ────────────────────────────────────
388	# T0 convergence aggregator (ADR-040 §2/§5, #1137): collapses the must-pass gate
389	# set into ONE verdict. This is the cycle's exit_when source and the single
390	# merge-blocking construct in the decomposed pipeline. verdict-in-artifact.
391	gate-aggregator:
392	  gate: auto
393	  roles: [gate_aggregator]
394	  io:
395	    destinations: [file, stdout]
396	    tail_lines: 200
397	
398	# ─── review_lenses (map group, ADVISORY) ─────────────────────────────────────
399	# issue #1295 (ADR-047 §2): converted from `type: parallel` to `type: map`.
400	# Each element (security, performance, red-team, correctness, scope) becomes one
401	# work unit dispatched to the review-lens plugin (provides.role: review_lens).
402	# `as: ZBUILD_REVIEW_LENS_ID` maps each element into the env var the review-lens
403	# plugin already reads to derive the lens identity — so the plugin is unchanged
404	# from its per-stage form. This eliminates the five separate lens-* stage
405	# definitions while preserving the same five isolated LLM calls and the same
406	# lens-<element>.json artifact names (ADR-038 §2 isolated-call discipline).
407	#
408	# aggregate: advisory — this group is NEVER on a merge-blocking path (ADR-040 §4).
409	# Convergence is owned by the build_test_cycle's gate-aggregator exit_when above;
410	# the B5 (#1137) no-LLM-on-convergence-path invariant therefore holds.
411	review_lenses:
412	  type: map
413	  over: lenses
414	  # ADR-051 §2: each lens names the persona it runs as; none is inferred
415	  # from the lens's name.
416	  elements:
417	    - id: security
418	      persona: security
419	    - id: performance
420	      persona: performance
421	    - id: red-team
422	      persona: red-team
423	    - id: correctness
424	      persona: correctness
425	    - id: scope
426	      persona: scope
427	    - id: sre
428	      persona: sre
429	  roles: [review_lens]
430	  as: ZBUILD_REVIEW_LENS_ID
431	  max_parallel: 4
432	  on_member_error: continue
433	  aggregate: advisory
434	  io:
435	    destinations: [file]
436	    tail_lines: 200
437	  router:
438	    timeout_s: 300
439	    max_turns: 25
440	
441	# ─── review-aggregator (leaf, ADVISORY) ──────────────────────────────────────
442	# C2 (#1141, ADR-040 §3/§4): merges the review_lenses members' results — the
443	# lens_result set the engine hands it (ADR-055 §1.4, #1842) — into ONE advisory
444	# merge-readiness report (review-report.json + review-report.md). Does NO LLM call
445	# — it merges lens JSON only. Bound by role review_aggregator to
446	# plugins/agent/review-aggregator. Requires lens_result: with no lens result the
447	# engine refuses it, and an empty set reports needs_attention, never "ready"
448	# (#1753). Never recommends a merge action, never blocks.
449	# The report.json filename is unchanged, so merge / pr-delivery consume it as before.
450	review-aggregator:
451	  gate: auto
452	  roles: [review_aggregator]
453	  io:
454	    destinations: [file, stdout]
455	    tail_lines: 200
456	
457	# ─── pr (leaf) ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
458	# T0 tool stage (ADR-013): opens the pull request; no LLM call.
459	pr:
460	  gate: auto
461	  roles: [pr]
462	  io:
463	    destinations: [file, stdout]
464	    tail_lines: 200
465	
466	# ─── release (always-run, ADR-054 §7) ────────────────────────────────────────
467	# Frees live resources — process groups, locks, handles — and DELETES NOTHING,
468	# so a failed run keeps every byte of its evidence on disk. The teardown plugin
469	# pins its own scope to `release`; `purge` is operator-only and unreachable from
470	# any run path (`zbuild clean --purge`).
471	#
472	# timeout_s is 30 and is load-bearing, not a formality: this stage runs inside
473	# the EXIT trap, so a cleanup hook that blocks would turn Ctrl-C into a hang —
474	# the exact class of bug the mechanism exists to prevent.
475	release:
476	  gate: auto
477	  roles: [teardown]
478	  router:
479	    timeout_s: 30
480	  io:
481	    destinations: [file]
482	    tail_lines: 50
483	
484	# ─── persist (always-run, ADR-050 §7 / ADR-059 §3) ───────────────────────────
485	# Snapshots the artifact area to zbuild/state/issue-<N> and PUSHES it, on every
486	# exit path. Runs AFTER release, and that order is load-bearing: release frees
487	# live resources and must stay fast, while this does network I/O and can block
488	# on auth or a dead remote. Persist last means a bad network can never delay an
489	# abort.
490	#
491	# timeout_s is 120, four times release's 30. A push crosses the network; a
492	# process-group kill does not.
493	persist:
494	  gate: auto
495	  roles: [persist]
496	  router:
497	    timeout_s: 120
498	  io:
499	    destinations: [file]
500	    tail_lines: 50
501	
502	# ─── hydrate (first in flow, ADR-050 §7 / ADR-059 §3) ────────────────────────
503	# Pulls prior artifacts for this issue out of zbuild/state/issue-<N> so each
504	# stage's prior-output seam can seed from earlier work. Runs BEFORE intake, and
505	# is NOT always-run — there is nothing to hydrate at the end of a run.
506	#
507	# It fetches origin's copy first, which is what makes a fresh CI clone able to
508	# restore at all; a LOCAL snapshot still wins on read, because it may carry work
509	# an earlier push never delivered.
510	hydrate:
511	  gate: auto
512	  roles: [hydrate]
513	  router:
514	    timeout_s: 60
515	  io:
516	    destinations: [file]
517	    tail_lines: 50
518

file.content:
id: simple
name: Simple Pipeline
extends: null

# ADR-037 §4: per-template merge policy. Wired to runtime behavior in #975.
merge_policy: auto_unless_flagged

defaults:
  strategy: map

# ─── Flow ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Simplified pipeline (ADR-037 EPIC #966 / ADR-040 EPIC #1129): 7 top-level flow
# units — intake, plan, design, build_test_cycle, review_lenses, review-aggregator,
# pr — where build_test_cycle groups the build/test leaves plus the decomposed
# mechanical gate stages, and review_lenses is the advisory lens group.
#
# I10-A..C historically wrapped build/test/objective-gate in build_test_cycle.
# B6 (#1138, ADR-040 — amends ADR-013/ADR-021/ADR-019; executes ADR-037 §6) CUT
# OVER convergence from the retired monolithic objective-gate to the composable
# mechanical gates + gate-aggregator; the objective-gate plugin was then removed
# in B7 (#1139). The single merge-blocking construct is the gate-aggregator
# verdict (ADR-040 §5), reached via the cycle's exit_when.
#
# C3 (#1142, ADR-040 §3 — supersedes ADR-038's single-stage fan-out; ADR-039
# parallel group; follows ADR-030 scope governance) CUTS OVER the lens side: the
# monolithic `review` stage (ADR-038's hand-rolled review-report fan-out, now
# UNREFERENCED here) is replaced by `review_lenses` — a `type: map over: lenses`
# `aggregate: advisory` group (issue #1295, ADR-047 §2; was `type: parallel`) —
# one work unit per lens element — followed by
# `review-aggregator`, which merges the per-lens results into ONE advisory
# merge-readiness report. The lens group is ADVISORY: it NEVER feeds the cycle's
# exit_when/convergence (that remains the gate-aggregator, ADR-040 §5) and never
# blocks merge. The B5 no-LLM-on-convergence-path invariant therefore holds.
flow:
  - hydrate
  - intake
  - plan
  - delivery_loop
  - review_lenses
  - review-aggregator
  - pr

# ─── always_run (#1831) ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Stages that run on EVERY exit path — success, non-zero rc, SIGINT, SIGTERM,
# timeout — in the order listed, after the flow has ended.
#
# This replaces a hardcoded dispatch in the runner's EXIT trap, which named one
# plugin by DIRECTORY (`plugins/tool/teardown`) and degraded silently to a no-op
# if it was absent. "Runs on every exit path" is a property of the FLOW, so it
# belongs in the template that defines the flow — not at a line number inside a
# 3000-line runner, where an edit can drop it without anything noticing. #1878
# found exactly that failure in the sibling mechanism: the snapshot was never
# called.
#
# An always-run stage is NOT part of `flow:` and never enters the flow's stage
# list: it has no place in the pipeline's data dependencies and must not affect
# convergence, verdicts, or the run's exit status.
#
# Each entry is an ordinary top-level stage section — resolved by `roles:` like
# any other stage, and bounded by its own `router.timeout_s`. A name here with
# no section, or a section with no `roles:`, REFUSES the template rather than
# quietly running nothing.
always_run:
  - release
  - persist

# ─── delivery_loop (cycle) — #2271, ADR-068 ─────────────────────────────────
# One outer loop holds the design loop and the build loop. Every stage sees
# every finding and says in its own result what it did about each; the engine
# never decides who owns a finding, and nothing jumps backwards.
#   - A design loop that runs out of rounds ends this round (build is skipped)
#     and this loop goes round. When this loop's rounds are spent, the run stops.
delivery_loop:
  type: cycle
  description: Design, then build, until both pass — going round when a finding needs design
  flow:
    - design_verify_cycle
    - build_test_cycle
  exit_when:
    all:
      - { stage: design_verify_cycle, field: verdict, op: eq, value: pass }
      - { stage: build_test_cycle, field: verdict, op: eq, value: pass }
  max_iterations: 2
  on_max: halt

# ─── design_verify_cycle (cycle) ─────────────────────────────────────────────
# ADR-046 (#1218, EPIC #1216): give the design stage an independent verifier that
# loops back TO it BEFORE the build cycle — so design/contract defects are caught
# where they are authored, not deep in the build cycle. Modelled on standard.yaml's
# design_impact_cycle (standard.yaml:40-67), which simple.yaml historically lacked.
#
# Members: design → design-gate. design-gate is a T0 tool (ADR-037 §3): a pure-grep
# PRE-build structural gate over design.md + the red-first stubs design writes. It
# is BOTH a cycle member AND convergence:gate, so the typed-aggregator preflight
# rule (A) is satisfied by binding exit_when directly to it — a single gate, no
# separate aggregator needed (contrast build_test_cycle's gate-aggregator, which
# rolls up MANY gates). exit_when fires on design-gate.verdict == pass.
# max_iterations: 2, on_max: halt (#2176): a contract the gate still rejects is
# not built. Nested in delivery_loop (#2271), running out of rounds ends that
# loop's round — build is skipped — and the outer loop goes round.
#
# Feedback: design.design → design.prior_design (self-edge) — mirrors
# design_impact_cycle so iter N+1 refines rather than re-creates (#773 lesson).
#
design_verify_cycle:
  type: cycle
  description: Verify the design contract is build-ready until design-gate passes
  flow:
    - design
    # #1683: does the design cover what the ISSUE asked for? Design is the only
    # reader of the issue, so nothing else confirms the SPECs are a faithful
    # statement of the ask. Inside the cycle, so a finding reaches design itself
    # on the next iteration.
    - spec-coverage
    - design-gate
  # #1284/ADR-047 multi-condition: BOTH must hold. spec-coverage may gate under
  # ADR-040 §5 as amended by #2040 — the standard it judges against is the
  # ISSUE, which design cannot re-author, so the only way to converge is to
  # actually cover it.
  #
  # `ne uncovered` rather than `eq covered`: `unreadable` must not stall the
  # cycle. intake writes a placeholder when the issue fetch fails (#1804), and
  # failing closed there would break every offline run for a condition that is
  # not design's fault. The finding still ships in the summary.
  exit_when:
    all:
      - { stage: design-gate, field: verdict, op: eq, value: pass }
      - { stage: spec-coverage, field: verdict, op: ne, value: uncovered }
  max_iterations: 2
  on_max: halt
  feedback:
    - from:
        stage: design
        output: design
      to:
        stage: design
        input: design
        required: false

# ─── spec-coverage (leaf, gate) ──────────────────────────────────────────────
# Model-judged but admissible on the convergence path (ADR-040 §5 / #2040): its
# standard is the issue, produced by intake OUTSIDE this cycle, so the judged
# party cannot re-author it.
spec-coverage:
  gate: auto
  roles: [spec_coverage]
  # A product owner asks "was what was asked for delivered?" — intent-seeking,
  # which is wrong for judging an assertion against a SPEC (the bug there
  # survives charity) and exactly right here, where the question IS about intent.
  persona: product-owner
  router:
    timeout_s: 600

# ─── test-author (leaf, advisory) ────────────────────────────────────────────
# ADR-040 §5: it makes a model call, so it may not sit on the convergence path.
# Its work is verified mechanically downstream — the test stage runs the
# assertions and acceptance-gate proves they discriminate.
test-author:
  gate: auto
  roles: [test_author]
  # #2188: no authored assertions → the cycle stops before build. Otherwise build
  # writes its own tests, the defect #2022 exists to prevent (#1849 run
  # 35949629759). Its failure is retried first (the stage's `retry:` budget).
  blocking: true
  router:
    # #2188: the same budget as build — authoring a 15–25 SPEC contract is
    # build-sized work (#1849: two 600s calls both timed out mid-write).
    # #2225: per CALL now — test-author loops until it says it is done, like
    # build, so a big contract takes more calls instead of overrunning one.
    # At most 4 calls: timeouts that are not back-to-back let the loop go on,
    # so the ceiling is calls × timeout — 60 min here (review #2229).
    timeout_s: 900
    max_turns: 0
    max_iterations: 4

# ─── spec-correspondence (leaf, advisory) ────────────────────────────────────
# ADR-040 §5: it makes a model call, so it may not gate. Its finding reaches
# test-author on the next iteration through the summary channel.
spec-correspondence:
  gate: auto
  roles: [spec_correspondence]
  # #1627: personas were consumed only by review lenses and NO template carried
  # a persona: key, so a persona manifest resolved to nothing. This is the first
  # stage-level binding. QA assures traceability; it does not test — which is
  # what separates it from test-strategist, whose instinct shown a mismatched
  # assertion is to repair it and answer yes.
  persona: quality-assurance
  router:
    timeout_s: 600

# ─── assertion-integrity (leaf, gate) ────────────────────────────────────────
# Mechanical, no model.route — so it MAY gate (ADR-040 §5).
assertion-integrity:
  gate: auto
  roles: [assertion_integrity]

# ─── issue-acceptance (leaf, gate) ───────────────────────────────────────────
# #1849: the finished change against the ISSUE. A model call on the convergence
# path is allowed for the same reason as spec-coverage (ADR-040 §5 as amended by
# #2040): its standard is the issue, which the judged stages cannot re-author.
issue-acceptance:
  gate: auto
  roles: [issue_acceptance]
  # Same question spec-coverage asks of the design — "was what was asked for
  # delivered?" — now asked of the code.
  persona: product-owner
  router:
    timeout_s: 600

# ─── build_test_cycle (cycle) ────────────────────────────────────────────────
# B6 (#1138, ADR-040 §2/§5): the cycle re-runs build/test then the decomposed
# mechanical gates (shape-floor, acceptance-gate, secret-scan) and finally the
# gate-aggregator, which collapses every must-pass gate into ONE convergence
# verdict. exit_when fires on gate-aggregator.verdict == pass — the ADR-019
# fail-closed contract re-expressed as a single composable construct (ADR-040 §5).
# (#1129 Change C, ADR-012: the lint/coverage/mutation read-out gates were
# DROPPED as cycle members — they were redundant. mutation and lint both run in
# the test suite (run-tests.sh --tier all / npm test, which the `test` cycle
# member runs), so a lint or mutation regression fails the `test` gate directly.
# coverage is NOT folded into the suite — it stays enforced by the dedicated CI
# `coverage` job (re-running it inside --tier all would trip the #983 re-entrancy
# guard; see ADR-012 "Coverage gating"). The lint-gate/coverage-gate/mutation-gate
# plugins remain canonical (ADR-013) but dormant for future reuse.)
# The individual gates are NON-blocking (no blocking:true):
# they emit verdict-in-artifact (ADR-004) and the cycle iterates-to-fix; the loop
# converges via exit_when, never via per-gate hard-blocks. max_iterations: 3.
# Nested in delivery_loop (#2271): running out of rounds hands back to that loop,
# which goes round from design.
build_test_cycle:
  type: cycle
  description: Build, test, and run the mechanical gates until gate-aggregator passes
  flow:
    # #2022: test-author runs FIRST. It authors the acceptance assertions from
    # the design's SPEC sentences before build implements against them, so the
    # code and the assertion are two independent readings rather than two
    # artifacts of one. It never sees the diff.
    - test-author
    # #2034: judges whether each assertion tests what its SPEC SAYS — the one
    # link execution cannot reach (a passing test proves the implementation
    # satisfies the ASSERTION, never that the assertion satisfies the SENTENCE).
    # Before build, because its question needs the requirement and the assertion
    # and not the implementation — which at this point does not exist yet, so
    # its isolation is a fact of placement rather than a rule to enforce.
    - spec-correspondence
    - build
    - test
    - shape-floor
    - acceptance-gate
    - secret-scan
    # #2022: mechanical backstop. The spawn denies build Edit() on the declared
    # TESTFILES, but #1919 P5 measured that a Write(...) deny rule matches
    # nothing — prevention is incomplete by construction. A fail here makes the
    # aggregate non-pass, so the cycle iterates rather than converging on a
    # rewritten assertion.
    - assertion-integrity
    # #1849: the finished change judged against the ISSUE, not the SPECs — the
    # only check after spec-coverage that reads the issue at all. A convergence
    # gate, so gate-aggregator's roster makes it must-pass; each unmet
    # requirement is a numbered finding.
    - issue-acceptance
    - gate-aggregator
  exit_when:
    stage: gate-aggregator
    field: verdict
    op: eq
    value: pass
  max_iterations: 3
  on_max: continue
  # The cycle CONVERGES rather than spinning build(no-op)→…→gate-aggregator(fail)
  # because the aggregator's consolidated gate-feedback.md reaches build. B2
  # (ADR-040): the gate-aggregator is the SINGLE collector of failure detail,
  # merging every failing mechanical gate into one document. It used to arrive
  # through a feedback: wire plus a bespoke reader; #1979 retired both — the
  # aggregator marks that output `summary: true` (#1976) and the engine injects
  # it, framed by verdict, with no per-consumer wiring.
# ─── intake (leaf) ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
intake:
  gate: auto
  roles: [intake]
  io:
    destinations: [file, stdout]
    tail_lines: 200

# ─── plan (leaf) ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
plan:
  gate: auto
  roles: [planner]
  # ADR-051: the provider runs the stage as this persona (--agent).
  persona: product-owner
  io:
    destinations: [file, stdout]
    tail_lines: 200
  router:
    timeout_s: 300
    # 45 (raised from the 25 default, #1442) — same starvation the impact stage
    # hit (#impact-max-turns): scope exploration needs headroom. The planner is
    # also told this budget in its prompt and biased to converge before it runs out.
    max_turns: 45

# ─── design (leaf, design_verify_cycle member) ───────────────────────────────
design:
  gate: auto
  roles: [designer]
  # ADR-051: the provider runs the stage as this persona (--agent).
  persona: architect
  io:
    destinations: [file, stdout]
    tail_lines: 200
  router:
    timeout_s: 600
    max_turns: 0

# ─── design-gate (leaf, design_verify_cycle member) ──────────────────────────
# T0 tool gate (ADR-046, #1218): PRE-build mechanical structural gate. Pure grep
# over design.md (NO LLM, NO baseline — ADR-037 §3). Runs the 5 structural
# checks (scope non-empty; acceptance block well-formed; every SPEC has a status
# — [code], [no-code] or [done] with evidence that exists (ADR-069); every [code]
# SPEC declares a TESTFILE; WIRING present/none + paths exist) and reports ALL
# violations in ONE pass. verdict-in-artifact; the design_verify_cycle exit_when
# reads design-gate.verdict == pass. Bound by role design_gate.
design-gate:
  gate: auto
  roles: [design_gate]
  io:
    destinations: [file, stdout]
    tail_lines: 200

# ─── build (leaf, cycle member) ──────────────────────────────────────────────
build:
  gate: auto
  roles: [builder]
  # ADR-051: the provider runs the stage as this persona (--agent).
  persona: developer
  io:
    destinations: [file, stdout]
    tail_lines: 200
  router:
    timeout_s: 900
    max_turns: 0

# ─── test (leaf, cycle member) ───────────────────────────────────────────────
test:
  gate: auto
  roles: [tester]
  io:
    destinations: [file, stdout]
    tail_lines: 200

# ─── shape-floor (leaf, cycle member) ────────────────────────────────────────
# T0 tool gate (ADR-040, #1134): un-gameable shape-floor check. verdict-in-artifact.
shape-floor:
  gate: auto
  roles: [shape_floor]
  io:
    destinations: [file, stdout]
    tail_lines: 200

# ─── acceptance-gate (leaf, cycle member) ────────────────────────────────────
# Mechanical (non-LLM) acceptance-contract gate (ADR-036, #922). No-op pass when
# the design acceptance block is absent (its design input is required:false in the
# manifest — design already emits the SPEC/WIRING block). Its gate_result feeds
# the acceptance→build feedback edge above.
# ADR-036 #1188: negctl_timeout_s bounds each SPEC negative-control / reachability
# test run (seconds). A timeout is classified INFRA (non-terminal), never a
# violation. Override per-run with ZBUILD_NEGCTL_TIMEOUT (env wins).
acceptance-gate:
  gate: auto
  roles: [acceptance_gate]
  negctl_timeout_s: 60
  io:
    destinations: [file, stdout]
    tail_lines: 200
  router:
    timeout_s: 600
    max_turns: 10

# ─── secret-scan (leaf, cycle member) ────────────────────────────────────────
# T0 tool gate (ADR-040, #1136): blocks hardcoded secrets/.env in the diff.
# verdict-in-artifact (skip on empty diff).
secret-scan:
  gate: auto
  roles: [secret_scan]
  io:
    destinations: [file, stdout]
    tail_lines: 200

# ─── gate-aggregator (leaf, cycle member) ────────────────────────────────────
# T0 convergence aggregator (ADR-040 §2/§5, #1137): collapses the must-pass gate
# set into ONE verdict. This is the cycle's exit_when source and the single
# merge-blocking construct in the decomposed pipeline. verdict-in-artifact.
gate-aggregator:
  gate: auto
  roles: [gate_aggregator]
  io:
    destinations: [file, stdout]
    tail_lines: 200

# ─── review_lenses (map group, ADVISORY) ─────────────────────────────────────
# issue #1295 (ADR-047 §2): converted from `type: parallel` to `type: map`.
# Each element (security, performance, red-team, correctness, scope) becomes one
# work unit dispatched to the review-lens plugin (provides.role: review_lens).
# `as: ZBUILD_REVIEW_LENS_ID` maps each element into the env var the review-lens
# plugin already reads to derive the lens identity — so the plugin is unchanged
# from its per-stage form. This eliminates the five separate lens-* stage
# definitions while preserving the same five isolated LLM calls and the same
# lens-<element>.json artifact names (ADR-038 §2 isolated-call discipline).
#
# aggregate: advisory — this group is NEVER on a merge-blocking path (ADR-040 §4).
# Convergence is owned by the build_test_cycle's gate-aggregator exit_when above;
# the B5 (#1137) no-LLM-on-convergence-path invariant therefore holds.
review_lenses:
  type: map
  over: lenses
  # ADR-051 §2: each lens names the persona it runs as; none is inferred
  # from the lens's name.
  elements:
    - id: security
      persona: security
    - id: performance
      persona: performance
    - id: red-team
      persona: red-team
    - id: correctness
      persona: correctness
    - id: scope
      persona: scope
    - id: sre
      persona: sre
  roles: [review_lens]
  as: ZBUILD_REVIEW_LENS_ID
  max_parallel: 4
  on_member_error: continue
  aggregate: advisory
  io:
    destinations: [file]
    tail_lines: 200
  router:
    timeout_s: 300
    max_turns: 25

# ─── review-aggregator (leaf, ADVISORY) ──────────────────────────────────────
# C2 (#1141, ADR-040 §3/§4): merges the review_lenses members' results — the
# lens_result set the engine hands it (ADR-055 §1.4, #1842) — into ONE advisory
# merge-readiness report (review-report.json + review-report.md). Does NO LLM call
# — it merges lens JSON only. Bound by role review_aggregator to
# plugins/agent/review-aggregator. Requires lens_result: with no lens result the
# engine refuses it, and an empty set reports needs_attention, never "ready"
# (#1753). Never recommends a merge action, never blocks.
# The report.json filename is unchanged, so merge / pr-delivery consume it as before.
review-aggregator:
  gate: auto
  roles: [review_aggregator]
  io:
    destinations: [file, stdout]
    tail_lines: 200

# ─── pr (leaf) ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# T0 tool stage (ADR-013): opens the pull request; no LLM call.
pr:
  gate: auto
  roles: [pr]
  io:
    destinations: [file, stdout]
    tail_lines: 200

# ─── release (always-run, ADR-054 §7) ────────────────────────────────────────
# Frees live resources — process groups, locks, handles — and DELETES NOTHING,
# so a failed run keeps every byte of its evidence on disk. The teardown plugin
# pins its own scope to `release`; `purge` is operator-only and unreachable from
# any run path (`zbuild clean --purge`).
#
# timeout_s is 30 and is load-bearing, not a formality: this stage runs inside
# the EXIT trap, so a cleanup hook that blocks would turn Ctrl-C into a hang —
# the exact class of bug the mechanism exists to prevent.
release:
  gate: auto
  roles: [teardown]
  router:
    timeout_s: 30
  io:
    destinations: [file]
    tail_lines: 50

# ─── persist (always-run, ADR-050 §7 / ADR-059 §3) ───────────────────────────
# Snapshots the artifact area to zbuild/state/issue-<N> and PUSHES it, on every
# exit path. Runs AFTER release, and that order is load-bearing: release frees
# live resources and must stay fast, while this does network I/O and can block
# on auth or a dead remote. Persist last means a bad network can never delay an
# abort.
#
# timeout_s is 120, four times release's 30. A push crosses the network; a
# process-group kill does not.
persist:
  gate: auto
  roles: [persist]
  router:
    timeout_s: 120
  io:
    destinations: [file]
    tail_lines: 50

# ─── hydrate (first in flow, ADR-050 §7 / ADR-059 §3) ────────────────────────
# Pulls prior artifacts for this issue out of zbuild/state/issue-<N> so each
# stage's prior-output seam can seed from earlier work. Runs BEFORE intake, and
# is NOT always-run — there is nothing to hydrate at the end of a run.
#
# It fetches origin's copy first, which is what makes a fresh CI clone able to
# restore at all; a LOCAL snapshot still wins on read, because it may carry work
# an earlier push never delivered.
hydrate:
  gate: auto
  roles: [hydrate]
  router:
    timeout_s: 60
  io:
    destinations: [file]
    tail_lines: 50

main() {
    local issue="" goal="" dry_run=false template="simple"
    local resume_mode=false from_stage="" no_resume=false force=false

                goal="$2"; shift 2 ;;
            --template)

            --dry-run)    dry_run=true;    shift ;;
            --resume)     resume_mode=true; shift ;;
            --no-resume)  no_resume=true;  shift ;;
            --force)      force=true;      shift ;;
            --self-host)  self_host=true;  shift ;;
            --from-stage)
                [[ -z "${2:-}" ]] && { error "--from-stage requires a value"; _usage; return 1; }
                from_stage="$2"; shift 2 ;;
            --help|-h)  _usage; return 0 ;;
            *) error "Unknown argument: $1"; _usage; return 1 ;;
        esac
    done

    # #963: ZBUILD_SELF_HOST=1 is equivalent to the --self-host flag.
    [[ "${ZBUILD_SELF_HOST:-0}" == "1" ]] && self_host=true
    # #2225: the run's resume intent reaches every stage as ZBUILD_RESUME —
    # 1 (reuse prior work) unless --no-resume, and ZBUILD_RESUME=0 in the
    # environment is the same as the flag. Each stage decides what reuse means
    # for it; hydrate restores nothing under 0.
    ZBUILD_RESUME="$(_runner_resume_intent "$no_resume")"

    [[ "$ZBUILD_RESUME" == "0" ]] && no_resume=true

    if [[ -z "$issue" && -z "$goal" ]]; then
        error "Must specify --issue <N> or --goal \"<text>\""

    fi

    # 6,338 awk spawns per run (~13s of 27s); most call sites read it inside $( ),

    # the fill has to happen in a shell that every later subshell descends from.
    # Cheap no-op when the cache is disabled or the root does not exist.

    # run roots its state under runs/<run_id>/ so concurrent runs never share a
    # state dir / artifacts. Explicit overrides (tests, CLI resume) win and skip
    # the re-root. Resolved here; applied once run_id is known (fresh-start block).
    local _state_is_default=false
    [[ -z "${ZBUILD_STATE_DIR:-}" && -z "${ZBUILD_STATE_FILE:-}" ]] && _state_is_default=true

    # Per-repo overrides live under the target repo's working tree (#653/#724
    # Copilot finding): use $PWD, not $_ZBUILD_ROOT (the install tree).
    if ! template_file="$(resolve_template_file "$template" "$PWD" 2>&1)"; then
        error "$template_file"
        return 1
    fi

    # Placed before --dry-run so dry-run also surfaces mismatches.
    # Fail-closed on corrupt state files (rather than letting get_state_field

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# scripts/lib/abort-propagation.sh — ADR-025 abort-propagation contract (Wave 15-B, #684)
#
# An abort is RECORDED once, as a word, and every dispatcher asks for it at the
# same two points in its loop (#1850, ADR-054 §4 — no rc carries the reason):
#
#   loop {
#       _zbuild_check_abort || return 1             # pre-flight
#       dispatch_child
#       _zbuild_propagate_abort $? || return 1      # post-flight
#   }
#
# Words: sigint | sigterm | cycle_abort | llm_unavailable | llm_rate_limited |
# scope_too_large. The first recorded abort wins.
#
# Two channels hold the word: `_ZB_ABORT_REASON` in this process, and the
# sentinel file ${ZBUILD_STATE_DIR}/.abort.signal, which crosses subshells and
# `_zbuild_make_fresh_shell` env scrubs (ADR-024) where a variable does not.
# An EMPTY sentinel reads as `sigint` — what arming wrote before it took a word.
#
# Sourced library: no `set -euo pipefail` (would mutate caller options).

[[ -n "${_ZBUILD_ABORT_PROP_LOADED:-}" ]] && return 0
_ZBUILD_ABORT_PROP_LOADED=1

# Empty when ZBUILD_STATE_DIR is unset: the helpers then keep the word in-process
# only, rather than fabricate a path under cwd.
_zbuild_abort_sentinel_path() {
    if [[ -n "${ZBUILD_STATE_DIR:-}" ]]; then
        printf '%s/.abort.signal' "$ZBUILD_STATE_DIR"
    fi
}

_zbuild_abort_reason() {
    if [[ -n "${_ZB_ABORT_REASON:-}" ]]; then
        printf '%s' "$_ZB_ABORT_REASON"
        return 0
    fi
    local _sentinel _word=""
    _sentinel="$(_zbuild_abort_sentinel_path)"
    [[ -n "$_sentinel" && -e "$_sentinel" ]] || return 0
    IFS= read -r _word 2>/dev/null < "$_sentinel" || true
    printf '%s' "${_word:-sigint}"
}

# Best-effort: a failed sentinel write must not fail a signal trap — the
# in-process word still holds the abort.
_zbuild_arm_abort_sentinel() {
    local _word="${1:-sigint}" _sentinel _dir _prior
    _prior="$(_zbuild_abort_reason)"
    if [[ -n "$_prior" ]]; then
        _ZB_ABORT_REASON="$_prior"
        return 0
    fi
    _ZB_ABORT_REASON="$_word"
    _sentinel="$(_zbuild_abort_sentinel_path)"
    [[ -z "$_sentinel" ]] && return 0
    _dir="$(dirname "$_sentinel")"
    [[ -d "$_dir" ]] || mkdir -p "$_dir" 2>/dev/null || return 0
    printf '%s\n' "$_word" > "$_sentinel" 2>/dev/null || true
    return 0
}

# Called by the runner's EXIT trap and by --resume, so a later run in the same
# state dir does not see a stale abort.
_zbuild_disarm_abort_sentinel() {
    local _sentinel
    unset _ZB_ABORT_REASON
    _sentinel="$(_zbuild_abort_sentinel_path)"
    [[ -z "$_sentinel" ]] && return 0
    [[ -e "$_sentinel" ]] && rm -f "$_sentinel" 2>/dev/null || true
    return 0
}

# Returns 1 so a caller can write `_zbuild_abort <word>; return` or `|| return 1`.
_zbuild_abort() {
    _zbuild_arm_abort_sentinel "${1:-sigint}"
    return 1
}

_zbuild_check_abort() {
    [[ -n "$(_zbuild_abort_reason)" ]] && return 1
    return 0
}

# 1 only when the child failed AND an abort is recorded: an ordinary failure is
# the caller's to handle, and a child that succeeded is not an abort.
_zbuild_propagate_abort() {
    [[ "${1:-0}" == "0" ]] && return 0
    _zbuild_check_abort
}

    # The run ends on a recorded abort (ADR-025); the word says how — it used to

    #   sigint | sigterm | cycle_abort → status interrupted.
    _runner_end_on_abort() {
        local _ea_state="$1" _ea_unit="$2" _ea_word _ea_detail="${_RUNNER_LLM_ABORT_DETAIL:-}"
        _ea_word="$(_zbuild_abort_reason)"
        _ea_word="${_ea_word:-sigint}"
        case "$_ea_word" in
            llm_unavailable|llm_rate_limited|scope_too_large)

                    "run_id=$_runner_run_id" "issue=$_runner_issue" \

2	# scripts/lib/stage-limits.sh — the limits a stage's model calls run under.
3	#
4	# One copy, two readers: the router enforces these numbers on every call
5	# (core/router/route.sh) and the engine states them to the stage in its rules
6	# (scripts/lib/stage-prompt.sh, ADR-067 §8). A stage told a different budget
7	# from the one it is killed at works until it is killed.
8	#
9	# Sourced library: inherits the caller's shell options; do NOT add set -euo.
10	[[ -n "${_ZBUILD_STAGE_LIMITS_LOADED:-}" ]] && return 0
11	_ZBUILD_STAGE_LIMITS_LOADED=1
12	
13	if ! declare -F manifest_router_knob >/dev/null 2>&1; then
14	    # shellcheck source=../../core/plugin-registry/manifest-router-budget.sh
15	    source "$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/../.." && pwd)/core/plugin-registry/manifest-router-budget.sh" 2>/dev/null || true
16	fi
17	
18	# ─── _route_manifest_knob <knob> — ADR-017 §11 (#1816) manifest layer ───────
19	# The dispatched plugin's OWN declared default, read from its manifest via the
20	# dispatch identity the engine exports at plugin_hook_call (ZBUILD_PLUGIN_DIR,
21	# ADR-054 §3 / #1862). Empty whenever there is no dispatch, no manifest, no
22	# declaration — or a declaration this router cannot use.
23	#
24	# Out-of-range and non-numeric values are IGNORED here, not fatal: the loud
25	# gate is validate_manifest at load, and a plugin that got past it with a bad
26	# value must fall back to the constant rather than hand the router a 0-second
27	# timeout. Fail-safe on the hot path, fail-loud at the boundary.
28	_route_manifest_knob() {
29	    local knob="$1"
30	    local dir="${ZBUILD_PLUGIN_DIR:-}"
31	    [[ -n "$dir" && -f "$dir/manifest.yaml" ]] || return 0
32	    declare -F manifest_router_knob >/dev/null 2>&1 || return 0
33	    local v; v="$(manifest_router_knob "$dir/manifest.yaml" "$knob" 2>/dev/null || true)"
34	    [[ "$v" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] || return 0
35	    local range; range="$(_manifest_router_range "$knob" 2>/dev/null || true)"
36	    [[ -n "$range" ]] || return 0
37	    local min="${range% *}" max="${range#* }"
38	    [[ "$v" -ge "$min" && "$v" -le "$max" ]] || return 0
39	    printf '%s' "$v"
40	}

42	# ─── _route_resolve_knob — ADR-017 (#455) precedence chokepoint ──────────────
43	# Generic helper: future knobs (tier_default, budget_usd, model_override) reuse
44	# this. Accessor returns per-stage value or empty; env_var supplies session-wide
45	# fallback; manifest_knob (#1816) names the plugin's own declared default; the
46	# compile-time constant is the floor:
47	#
48	#   template accessor  >  env var  >  manifest config.router.*  >  constant
49	#
50	# The manifest sits BELOW env and template because it is a default, not an
51	# override: a flow may right-size a stage for a fast lane, and the operator
52	# escape hatch must still beat both. It sits ABOVE the constant because that is
53	# what the constant always was — a default nobody could state per stage.
54	_route_resolve_knob() {
55	    local accessor_fn="$1" env_var="$2" default_val="$3"
56	    local override_event="${4:-router.timeout.override_ignored}"
57	    local manifest_knob="${5:-}"
58	    local v=""
59	    if [[ -n "${ZBUILD_CURRENT_STAGE:-}" ]] && declare -F "$accessor_fn" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
60	        v="$($accessor_fn "$ZBUILD_CURRENT_STAGE" 2>/dev/null || true)"
61	    fi
62	    if [[ -n "$v" ]]; then
63	        # If env var ALSO set and differs, emit override-ignored event for audit.
64	        # A manifest value losing to template or env is NOT this case: a default
65	        # being replaced is the design, and eventing it would make every
66	        # declaring plugin noisy on every dispatch.
67	        local env_val="${!env_var:-}"
68	        if [[ -n "$env_val" && "$env_val" != "$v" ]]; then
69	            eb_emit_event "$override_event" \
70	                "stage=${ZBUILD_CURRENT_STAGE:-}" \
71	                "env_var=$env_var" \
72	                "env_value=$env_val" \
73	                "applied=$v" 2>/dev/null || true
74	        fi
75	        printf '%s\n' "$v"; return 0
76	    fi
77	    local env_v="${!env_var:-}"
78	    if [[ -n "$env_v" ]]; then
79	        printf '%s\n' "$env_v"; return 0
80	    fi
81	    if [[ -n "$manifest_knob" ]]; then
82	        local mv; mv="$(_route_manifest_knob "$manifest_knob")"
83	        if [[ -n "$mv" ]]; then
84	            printf '%s\n' "$mv"; return 0
85	        fi
86	    fi
87	    printf '%s\n' "$default_val"

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# scripts/lib/stage-limits.sh — the limits a stage's model calls run under.
#
# One copy, two readers: the router enforces these numbers on every call
# (core/router/route.sh) and the engine states them to the stage in its rules
# (scripts/lib/stage-prompt.sh, ADR-067 §8). A stage told a different budget
# from the one it is killed at works until it is killed.
#
# Sourced library: inherits the caller's shell options; do NOT add set -euo.
[[ -n "${_ZBUILD_STAGE_LIMITS_LOADED:-}" ]] && return 0
_ZBUILD_STAGE_LIMITS_LOADED=1

if ! declare -F manifest_router_knob >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    # shellcheck source=../../core/plugin-registry/manifest-router-budget.sh
    source "$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/../.." && pwd)/core/plugin-registry/manifest-router-budget.sh" 2>/dev/null || true
fi

# ─── _route_manifest_knob <knob> — ADR-017 §11 (#1816) manifest layer ───────
# The dispatched plugin's OWN declared default, read from its manifest via the
# dispatch identity the engine exports at plugin_hook_call (ZBUILD_PLUGIN_DIR,
# ADR-054 §3 / #1862). Empty whenever there is no dispatch, no manifest, no
# declaration — or a declaration this router cannot use.
#
# Out-of-range and non-numeric values are IGNORED here, not fatal: the loud
# gate is validate_manifest at load, and a plugin that got past it with a bad
# value must fall back to the constant rather than hand the router a 0-second
# timeout. Fail-safe on the hot path, fail-loud at the boundary.
_route_manifest_knob() {
    local knob="$1"
    local dir="${ZBUILD_PLUGIN_DIR:-}"
    [[ -n "$dir" && -f "$dir/manifest.yaml" ]] || return 0
    declare -F manifest_router_knob >/dev/null 2>&1 || return 0
    local v; v="$(manifest_router_knob "$dir/manifest.yaml" "$knob" 2>/dev/null || true)"
    [[ "$v" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] || return 0
    local range; range="$(_manifest_router_range "$knob" 2>/dev/null || true)"
    [[ -n "$range" ]] || return 0
    local min="${range% *}" max="${range#* }"
    [[ "$v" -ge "$min" && "$v" -le "$max" ]] || return 0
    printf '%s' "$v"
}

# ─── _route_resolve_knob — ADR-017 (#455) precedence chokepoint ──────────────
# Generic helper: future knobs (tier_default, budget_usd, model_override) reuse
# this. Accessor returns per-stage value or empty; env_var supplies session-wide
# fallback; manifest_knob (#1816) names the plugin's own declared default; the
# compile-time constant is the floor:
#
#   template accessor  >  env var  >  manifest config.router.*  >  constant
#
# The manifest sits BELOW env and template because it is a default, not an
# override: a flow may right-size a stage for a fast lane, and the operator
# escape hatch must still beat both. It sits ABOVE the constant because that is
# what the constant always was — a default nobody could state per stage.
_route_resolve_knob() {
    local accessor_fn="$1" env_var="$2" default_val="$3"
    local override_event="${4:-router.timeout.override_ignored}"
    local manifest_knob="${5:-}"
    local v=""
    if [[ -n "${ZBUILD_CURRENT_STAGE:-}" ]] && declare -F "$accessor_fn" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
        v="$($accessor_fn "$ZBUILD_CURRENT_STAGE" 2>/dev/null || true)"
    fi
    if [[ -n "$v" ]]; then
        # If env var ALSO set and differs, emit override-ignored event for audit.
        # A manifest value losing to template or env is NOT this case: a default
        # being replaced is the design, and eventing it would make every
        # declaring plugin noisy on every dispatch.
        local env_val="${!env_var:-}"
        if [[ -n "$env_val" && "$env_val" != "$v" ]]; then
            eb_emit_event "$override_event" \
                "stage=${ZBUILD_CURRENT_STAGE:-}" \
                "env_var=$env_var" \
                "env_value=$env_val" \
                "applied=$v" 2>/dev/null || true
        fi
        printf '%s\n' "$v"; return 0
    fi
    local env_v="${!env_var:-}"
    if [[ -n "$env_v" ]]; then
        printf '%s\n' "$env_v"; return 0
    fi
    if [[ -n "$manifest_knob" ]]; then
        local mv; mv="$(_route_manifest_knob "$manifest_knob")"
        if [[ -n "$mv" ]]; then
            printf '%s\n' "$mv"; return 0
        fi
    fi
    printf '%s\n' "$default_val"
}

# Concrete: per-stage router.timeout_s > $ZBUILD_ROUTER_TIMEOUT >
# manifest config.router.timeout_s > 300s default.
_route_resolve_timeout() {
    _route_resolve_knob template_stage_router_timeout ZBUILD_ROUTER_TIMEOUT 300 \
        router.timeout.override_ignored timeout_s
}

# ADR-018 (#466): per-stage router.max_turns > $ZBUILD_ROUTER_MAX_TURNS > 25 default.
# ADR-029 G3 (#812): when the cycle orchestrator detects a router timeout for
# this stage, it sets ZBUILD_ROUTER_MAX_TURNS_OVERRIDE so the next dispatch
# of the same stage uses an escalated budget (+50%, capped at 2× base). The
# override wins over the per-stage template AND the env knob because that's
# the entire point — escalation must beat the static config that already
# proved too small.
_route_resolve_max_turns() {
    if [[ "${ZBUILD_ROUTER_MAX_TURNS_OVERRIDE:-}" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]]; then
        printf '%s' "$ZBUILD_ROUTER_MAX_TURNS_OVERRIDE"
        return 0
    fi
    _route_resolve_knob template_stage_router_max_turns ZBUILD_ROUTER_MAX_TURNS 25 \
        router.max_turns.override_ignored max_turns
}

# ADR-018 Amendment N (#762): when max_turns resolves to the 0 sentinel,
# classify which source set it (template > env > manifest > default) for
# telemetry. Emits `template`, `env`, `manifest` (#1816), or `default`. The
# `default` branch is currently unreachable (compile-time default is 25, not 0)
# but kept for forward compatibility if the default ever changes.
# Copilot review #764: compare numerically so "00", "000" etc. (accepted
# by the ^[0-9]+$ validator) classify correctly.
_route_classify_max_turns_source() {
    local _tpl_val=""
    if [[ -n "${ZBUILD_CURRENT_STAGE:-}" ]] \
        && command -v template_stage_router_max_turns >/dev/null 2>&1; then
        _tpl_val="$(template_stage_router_max_turns "$ZBUILD_CURRENT_STAGE" 2>/dev/null || true)"
    fi
    local _mf_val; _mf_val="$(_route_manifest_knob max_turns)"
    if [[ "$_tpl_val" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] && [[ "$_tpl_val" -eq 0 ]]; then
        printf '%s' "template"
    elif [[ "${ZBUILD_ROUTER_MAX_TURNS:-}" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] && [[ "${ZBUILD_ROUTER_MAX_TURNS}" -eq 0 ]]; then
        printf '%s' "env"
    elif [[ "$_mf_val" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] && [[ "$_mf_val" -eq 0 ]]; then
        # #1816: a plugin that declares `max_turns: 0` owns that sentinel. Left
        # unclassified it would be recorded as `default`, which is the one thing
        # it is not — the record would name a source that declared nothing.
        printf '%s' "manifest"
    else
        printf '%s' "default"
    fi
}

# ADR-018 (#467): per-stage router.max_iterations > $ZBUILD_ROUTER_MAX_ITERATIONS > 10 default.
_route_resolve_max_iterations() {
    _route_resolve_knob template_stage_router_max_iterations ZBUILD_ROUTER_MAX_ITERATIONS 10 \
        router.max_iterations.override_ignored
}

# ADR-029 (#1230): per-stage router.retries > $ZBUILD_ROUTER_RETRIES > 0 default.
# The count of retry-on-timeout (rc=124) attempts BEFORE the verbatim-124
# fallback. Default 0 (opt-in). Honored by BOTH leaf paths — single-shot
# (_route_call_claude) and agentic-loop (route_to_model_loop) — so every leaf
# node respects the knob wherever it sits. Out-of-range values (validator
# already bounds template 0..10; env is unbounded) clamp to 0 fail-safe.
_route_resolve_retries() {
    local v; v="$(_route_resolve_knob template_stage_router_retries ZBUILD_ROUTER_RETRIES 0 \
        router.retries.override_ignored retries)"
    if [[ "$v" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] && [[ "$v" -ge 0 ]] && [[ "$v" -le 10 ]]; then
        printf '%s' "$v"
    else
        printf '0'
    fi
}

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Integration test (#1829, ADR-054 §7): the runner dispatches cleanup(release)
# on EVERY exit path from a run — success, non-zero rc, the SIGINT propagation
# chain, an external SIGTERM, and an external timeout.
#
# This is the acceptance criterion the mechanism exists for: a stage's live
# resources must be freed however the run ends. A single missed exit path leaks
# whatever that stage spawned (#1748: suites observed alive 15+ min after exit).
#
# Why SIGINT is driven by the stage rather than `kill -INT`: this harness starts
# non-interactively with SIGINT inherited as SIG_IGN, and POSIX forbids a child
# from un-ignoring it — so `kill -INT` is silently dropped and the assertion
# would pass standalone while proving nothing. The repo's existing
# sigint-aborts-pipeline-test.sh drives the same chain the same way: the child
# returns 130, which is exactly what the kernel produces on Ctrl-C. Since #1850
# (ADR-054 §4, ADR-025) a signal is a recorded WORD, not an rc, so the stage
# also arms the abort sentinel (empty = sigint), as the runner's INT trap in
# the process group would.
#
# Assertion in every case: the stub stages' cleanup hooks recorded `release`
# (and never `purge`) in the marker file.
set -euo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
REPO_ROOT="$(cd "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)"
RUNNER="$REPO_ROOT/core/pipeline/runner.sh"

# shellcheck source=../../scripts/lib/helpers.sh
source "$REPO_ROOT/scripts/lib/helpers.sh"
# shellcheck source=../../scripts/lib/test-helpers.sh
source "$REPO_ROOT/scripts/lib/test-helpers.sh"

print_test_header "runner dispatches cleanup(release) on every exit path (#1829)"
setup_test_env "runner-release-exit-paths"
export ZBUILD_CONTRACT_VALIDATOR=warn

PLUGINS_ROOT="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/plugins"
export ZBUILD_PLUGINS_ROOT="$PLUGINS_ROOT"
export ZBUILD_EVENT_SCHEMA="$REPO_ROOT/config/event-schema.json"
export ZBUILD_MODELS_FILE="$REPO_ROOT/config/models.json"
export ZBUILD_CYCLES_ENABLED=0
mkdir -p "$PLUGINS_ROOT"

# The teardown plugin resolves its repo root by walking three levels up from
# its own directory (plugin-bootstrap), using a LOGICAL pwd — so symlinking the
# plugin itself would resolve to TEST_TEMP_DIR and fail to find helpers.sh.
# Give TEST_TEMP_DIR the shape of a repo root instead, then copy teardown in.
ln -s "$REPO_ROOT/scripts" "$TEST_TEMP_DIR/scripts"
ln -s "$REPO_ROOT/core"    "$TEST_TEMP_DIR/core"
mkdir -p "$PLUGINS_ROOT/tool"
cp -R "$REPO_ROOT/plugins/tool/teardown" "$PLUGINS_ROOT/tool/teardown"

mock_plugin_factory "intake" "agent" 0 >/dev/null
mock_plugin_factory "build"  "agent" 0 >/dev/null
mock_plugin_factory "test"   "tool"  0 >/dev/null

# Declare the optional cleanup hook — without it plugin_hook_call emits
# `plugin.cleanup.absent`, returns 0 (#1823: rc is binary), and the stage is a
# no-op rather than a witness.
# Re-emit the manifest rather than appending: `cleanup:` has to sit inside the
# contiguous `hooks:` block, and mock_plugin_factory already wrote `requires:`
# after it. #1850: the re-emitted manifest keeps the factory's v2 declaration —
# result_contract 2 and a JSON primary each run hook below writes.
for _spec in "agent/intake:intake:intake_cleanup" "agent/build:build:build_cleanup" "tool/test:test:test_cleanup"; do

id: $_id
name: Test $_id
kind: $_kind
version: 0.0.1
hooks:
  run: ${_id//-/_}_run
  cleanup: $_fn
requires:
  core:
    - redaction
provides:
  result_contract: 2
outputs:
